cands.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 44th District since January 2017. Graduated from UCLA (2000) and USC law school (2005). Served on the Hermosa Beach city council and as mayor pro tempore. Worked as an adviser to large and small businesses. Youngest of eleven children of Mexican immigrants.

endorsements.text: California Federation of Labor Unions, AFL-CIO (2026 endorsement)

cands.gaps: We could not find where Barragán was born or when her family settled in California; the sources say only that she grew up in Carson. We found no documented statements or actions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, school choice, abortion, gun policy or police pay. We found no documented position on specific development or growth projects, no controversies, and no foreign ties. The years she served on the Hermosa Beach city council were not given. Her campaign issues text is from 2016, and she did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys in recent cycles.

cands.name: Genevieve Angel

money.note: Individuals gave $18,826; PAC money $0; candidate's own money $3,000. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Family nurse practitioner, healthcare executive and small-business owner who has lived in Lakewood, California, for nearly 30 years. She moved to Southern California from Manila, Philippines. She has not held public office. Republican candidate for U.S. House, District 44, in 2026.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California, Reform California, and the LA GOP (the last per her own survey answer), plus several voter-guide recommendations listed on Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: Her birthplace and where she was raised are not stated in the pages we could read; they say only that she moved from Manila, Philippines. She has no record in public office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found no stated positions from her on data centers, property taxes, foreign or investor ownership of homes and land, growth and land conservation, H-1B visas, police pay and pensions, gun laws, or school choice and teacher pay. Her immigration platform is general ("secure borders, fair legal pathways") and gives no specifics. Her law study, her "Magna Cum Laude" honor and her work history come only from her own campaign site and survey answers, and we found no independent confirmation. We found no news coverage of controversies, and no photo or other documentation of foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 55: Her campaign site says she has lived in Lakewood for nearly 30 years after moving from Manila, Philippines, and she earned her nursing degree in 1992, so she arrived as an adult more than 25 years ago.

score.why: Raised $21.8k, under $50,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Family nurse practitioner and senior healthcare executive with experience in hospitals, health plans and community services, and a small-business owner. She has held no elected or appointed government office.
qual.why: Her executive and business management background fits the middle band. She has no legislative, budget-office or prosecutorial experience, and the campaign site's claim of two years of law study is not a completed degree.
qual.label: Her executive and business management background fits the middle band. She has no legislative, budget-office or prosecutorial experience, and the campaign site's claim of two years of law study is not a completed degree.

clean-money.evidence: Her campaign site says the campaign is "powered by people — not corporate money." This is a campaign claim, not a documented pledge to refuse specific donors.

pro-life.evidence: In a March 8, 2026 Ballotpedia survey response she listed "Right to Life" among the policy areas she is passionate about. The final March 23 version of her response no longer lists it.
